# Context Performance Benchmarks

Dimension 8 of the LLM Token Budgeting research. Covers how context utilization
affects output quality, latency vs context size, and diminishing returns.
Source details in [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Lost in the Middle (Liu et al. 2023)

The seminal finding: U-shaped performance curve where models perform best when
relevant information is at the beginning or end of context, significantly worse
in the middle [7]. Tested on multi-document QA and key-value retrieval. Even
explicitly long-context models exhibit this pattern [7].

## Context Rot (Chroma, 2025)

18 LLMs tested across 4 vendor families (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Alibaba) [13]:

| Context Length | Degradation |
|---------------|-------------|
| 25-100 words | Models perform well |
| 250-500 words | First position accuracy issues |
| 2,500+ words | Significant performance drops |

Key behavioral differences [13]:
- **Claude**: Most conservative; abstains when uncertain
- **GPT**: Highest hallucination rates with distractors
- **Gemini**: Generates random words starting at 500-750 tokens

Counterintuitive finding: models perform worse when haystack preserves logical
flow; shuffling the haystack consistently improves performance [13].

## RULER Benchmark (NVIDIA, 2024)

17 long-context LMs evaluated on 13 tasks beyond simple retrieval [8]:
- Only half of models claiming 32K+ context maintain satisfactory performance
  at 32K [8]
- Nearly perfect vanilla NIAH scores but large performance drops on complex
  tasks [8]
- Benchmark open-sourced for reproducibility [8]

## Context Length Alone Hurts Performance

Even with perfect retrieval, performance degrades 13.9%-85% as input length
increases [6]:

| Model | Task | Degradation at 30K tokens |
|-------|------|--------------------------|
| Llama-3.1-8B | MMLU | 24.2% accuracy drop |
| Llama-3.1-8B | HumanEval | 57.3% → 9.7% |
| Mistral-v0.3-7B | Variable Summation | 66% drop |

Degradation persists when [6]:
- Distraction tokens replaced with whitespace
- All irrelevant tokens masked during attention
- Evidence placed immediately before questions

This indicates input length itself undermines reasoning, independent of
retrieval quality [6].

## Effective vs Advertised Context Windows

| Concept | Finding | Source |
|---------|---------|--------|
| Maximum Effective Context | 60-70% of advertised maximum [45] | arXiv 2509.21361 |
| Gemini 2.5 Pro effective | ~200K despite larger advertised [45] | arXiv 2509.21361 |
| BABILong finding | Models degrade beyond 10% of input capacity [47] | NIAH framework |
| Practical recommendation | Use ~80% as soft ceiling [13][29] | Context rot, CDR |

## Latency vs Context Size

Dense transformer latency degradation with context length [9]:

| Model | 4K words | 10K words | 15K words |
|-------|----------|-----------|-----------|
| Llama-3.1-70B | 150.54% | 446.02% | 719.64% |
| Qwen1.5-14B | 324.56% | 434.39% | 701.03% |

Despite massive latency increases, accuracy decline was minimal: 98.5% → 98%
(Llama-3.1-70B), 99% → 97.5% (Qwen1.5-14B). The performance tax is operational
(latency) rather than cognitive (accuracy) [9].

**Root cause**: Attention scales O(n²) with sequence length. Memory bandwidth
and KV cache management are primary bottlenecks, not reasoning capability [9].

## Diminishing Returns Thresholds

Based on cross-source synthesis:
- **~40% context fill**: Where diminishing returns start, depending on task [13]
- **60-70%**: Maximum effective context for most models [45]
- **80%**: Recommended soft ceiling for production systems [29]
- **100%**: Hard failures, API errors, significant quality loss

**Operator review flag**: The 40% threshold is derived from a single source
and should be validated against specific use cases before relying on it for
production decisions.

## Implications for Token Budgeting

1. **Don't fill context windows** — effective capacity is 60-80% of advertised
2. **Budget for latency** — 7× latency increase at 15K words for 70B models [9]
3. **Position matters** — place critical information at start or end [7]
4. **Context overhead compounds** — stateless APIs resend full history each turn [27]
5. **Routing by context need** — use large-context models only when needed,
   cheaper models for short contexts

## Gaps and Limitations

- Precise mathematical relationship between fill percentage and degradation
  across architectures is not published
- Energy cost per token at different context sizes lacks published data
- Quality-adjusted cost-per-query comparing RAG (short context) vs native
  long context is not well benchmarked
- Multi-needle task degradation beyond 256K tokens has limited data
- The 40% inflection point for diminishing returns needs more validation
